BTC.note: Sold 2 Nov 2026 – no longer held; still watched for MSTR. Binance exchange hack (95% covered) and BTCPay hot-wallet drains; Bitcoin itself unaffected
BTC.detail: Binance (an exchange) lost about US$6.3bn on 29-30 Oct to North Korea-linked hackers; it was not a flaw in Bitcoin. Binance says about 95% is now replaced (BTC fully backed), withdrawals reopened in phases from 1 Nov (net outflow about US$3.6bn, 2.1% of assets), and a verifiable reserves proof is due about 3 Nov. The attacker's 18,270 stolen BTC have not moved. Separately, on 1 Nov (US time) BTCPay Server, open-source software merchants use to accept Bitcoin, told operators to shut down after reports of attackers draining hot wallets on several servers; cause and losses not yet confirmed; a core contributor says losses so far are on versions older than 2.4.2 and the latest releases appear unaffected. This hits merchants' online wallets, not the Bitcoin network. Bob sold his Bitcoin fund on 2 Nov 2026 and this is now tracked for MSTR's sake. Quantum: estimates keep falling but remain theoretical, hardware expected early 2030s.

TSLA.detail: No confirmed Tesla breach. A Sept 2026 hacking-forum claim is unverified.

MSTR.detail: Strategy itself was not hacked. The Binance hack only moved its share price through Bitcoin.

SEMI.detail: No breaches at SEMI's top holdings. Intel's Israel factory explosion is an operations issue, not a security one.
